title: KOD-78-AC-15 — Outbound admission classifies references and aggregate data before rendering
description:
**Check:** Known references are classified before rendering and generated tracker counts/rosters are checked from structured source data at the durable writer. The configurable regex engine and its aggregate prose heuristics are removed, with no alternative scanner framework added merely to relocate them. Every existing outbound path remains covered by an explicit CLEAN / REDACTED / BLOCKED decision.

**Do:** Replace RegexContentScanner and PatternOutboundContentGate with the smallest composition of reference classification, durable-write admission, deterministic credential checking and the existing semantic privacy judgment. Preserve the OutboundContentGate contract where consumers need it. Use a six-row in-code redaction verdict table, max-severity behavior and identifier-writer blocking. Trace authored and fetched strings as well as app-rendered references; deleting text inspection is permitted only where structured provenance or equivalent checking covers the input.

**Evidence:** Pending verification against the amended contract (branch/sha, real writer path, test names and results).

**Plan amendment · 2026-09-08:** Implements [KOD-744](<https://linear.app/duckburg/issue/KOD-744>). Previous scanner/configuration prescriptions are superseded; historical grooming comments do not verify this new contract. Preserve <issue id="f0d50751-a867-4a8b-a05f-48fbdb9fbc8b" href="https://linear.app/duckburg/issue/KOD-47/visibility-aware-output-sanitization-nothing-private-ever-lands-in-a">KOD-47</issue> visibility/error behavior and <issue id="ae6aa78c-f954-4a1a-acb9-a857fa8b759f" href="https://linear.app/duckburg/issue/KOD-106/agentic-outbound-content-scanner-the-judgment-half-of-the-outbound">KOD-106</issue> semantic privacy judgment for agent-authored and third-party text.

The existing six redaction categories suffice.

**Do:** Extend OperationConfig.private_surface into structured hosts/workspace slugs while retaining or migrating its existing semantic privacy description. Coordinate that shape with <issue id="0532a765-e9d8-4584-9ffe-e5897becf084" href="https://linear.app/duckburg/issue/KOD-139/operationconfig-is-three-concerns-in-one-model-operation-authority">KOD-139</issue>. Expose IssueKey/domain references parsed by the adapter; classify known references before rendering and tokenize URLs in agent-authored or fetched text through the same parser/classifier. Keep credentials in CREDENTIAL_SHAPES as code constants. Remove deny_patterns, deny_pattern_verdicts and the ORG_PRIVATE pattern-list rejection when the replacement covers all consumers.

**Evidence:** Pending verification against the amended contract (branch/sha, real writer path, test names and results).

**Plan amendment · 2026-09-08:** Implements [KOD-744](<https://linear.app/duckburg/issue/KOD-744>). Previous scanner/configuration prescriptions are superseded; historical grooming comments do not verify this new contract. Preserve <issue id="f0d50751-a867-4a8b-a05f-48fbdb9fbc8b" href="https://linear.app/duckburg/issue/KOD-47/visibility-aware-output-sanitization-nothing-private-ever-lands-in-a">KOD-47</issue> visibility/error behavior and <issue id="ae6aa78c-f954-4a1a-acb9-a857fa8b759f" href="https://linear.app/duckburg/issue/KOD-106/agentic-outbound-content-scanner-the-judgment-half-of-the-outbound">KOD-106</issue> semantic privacy judgment for agent-authored and third-party text.

title: KOD-78-AC-7 — An undemonstrable obligation never blocks: such a lane reaches scope_converged_with_residual
description:
**Check:** An undemonstrable obligation never blocks: a lane whose remaining obligations are all undemonstrable-here or owned elsewhere reaches `scope_converged_with_residual`, never `scope_stopped_short` and never a blocked terminal. (gen · M5-T2)
**Do:** Encode the terminal-side consequence of the Q1 fire-ruling on <issue id="7db77f39-4c85-48b0-8240-826917474e89" href="https://linear.app/duckburg/issue/KOD-78/v03-l6-scope-terminal-per-lane-outcome-vector-initiative-progress">KOD-78</issue>. A missing DEMONSTRATION routes to residual; it is a different condition from AC-8's missing WRITE, and the two must not be collapsed — routing one into the other lets a skipped write launder itself.
**Evidence:** — (sha · test names in tests/chains/test_scope_terminal.py · session/comment ids)

title: KOD-78-AC-8 — The terminal is never a first writer: an unreadable record becomes UNRECORDED_AT_TERMINAL and forbids convergence
description:
**Check:** The terminal is never a first writer: before emitting it re-reads every lane-vector entry and every residual item from its owning issue by the item's record reference, an item whose record cannot be read back is emitted as `UNRECORDED_AT_TERMINAL` naming the surface that owed the write, its presence forbids `scope_converged`, and the terminal neither writes the missing record nor omits the item — a missing write is never routed into the residual as a missing demonstration. (V · R15)
**Do:** Read every item back through the tracker port by its record reference — a criterion sub-issue key reads as that sub-issue's state and Evidence. Assert the fake tracker records zero writes from the terminal to the owing issue.
**Evidence:** — (sha · test names in tests/chains/test_scope_terminal.py · session/comment ids)

title: KOD-78-AC-9 — Write set closed: the terminal's only tracker write is the container status update
description:
**Check:** Write set closed: across every terminal fixture the tracker writes attributable to the terminal are exactly the container status update; any issue-surface write fails the fixture; and the container description surface this lane holds is never written by it. (V · R16, R13)
**Do:** Assert the fake tracker's write log attributable to the terminal over every fixture. The lane holds the container description precisely so nothing writes it. The evaluator's per-criterion state moves are the evaluator's writes, not the terminal's, and this criterion does not forbid them.
**Evidence:** — (sha · test names in tests/chains/test_scope_terminal.py · session/comment ids)

title: KOD-78-AC-10 — No machine outcome is a function of a merge: lanes holding open unmerged PRs are scope_converged
description:
**Check:** No machine outcome is a function of a merge: a fixture whose lanes all hold open, unmerged pull requests is `scope_converged`, while a lane holding no open pull request yields `scope_converged_with_residual` carrying a lane-without-open-PR item. (V · R14)
**Do:** Count a lane toward convergence when its terminal act is complete — an open PR whose checks the run watched — never on a merge, which is a human act outside the loop. Several PRs open at once, parallel or stacked, is the normal converged state.
**Evidence:** — (sha · test names in tests/chains/test_scope_terminal.py · session/comment ids)

title: KOD-78-AC-11 — Silence cannot render as success: reported entries cover the lanes dispatched, an unreported lane forbids convergence
description:

The lane-report vocabulary and the return-boundary assertion are consumed from the sibling issue that owns them; this lane defines neither. (gen · M5-T3)
**Do:** Assert arity at the evaluator's return boundary: entries reported equal lanes dispatched. Consume the unreported-lane reading from the sibling issue that owns it; define no vocabulary here.
**Evidence:** — (sha · test names in tests/chains/test_scope_terminal.py · session/comment ids). Blocked pending supply, never infeasible: that vocabulary and that return-boundary assertion are the sibling issue's deliverable and are absent at the comparison base. This stays Todo until the sibling sits on this lane's base; the Check text needs no edit.

title: KOD-78-AC-12 — Resumability: a prior attempt that left no terminal event is reported scope_stopped_short from durable state
description:

description:

**Do:** Use destination durability and typed count/roster data for generated content; count references at the writer, not by reparsing rendered issue keys. Carry or inspect authorship/provenance at free-text entry paths so an agent-authored count claim and roster receive equivalent admission. Use paired destination cases, including a zero-reference count claim, rather than numeral-distance or separator-regex tests.

title: KOD-110-AC-2 — Composition happens in a scratch worktree through the git port, in the planner's lane order, removed on every path
description:
**Check:** Composition happens in a scratch worktree obtained through the git port, with the lane head branches merged in the planner's lane order — asserted as the planner's order, not the order the pull requests were opened — and the worktree is removed on every path, including the raising one. (V · S1-U2)
**Do:** Obtain a scratch worktree per union attempt through the git port; merge the lane head branches in the planner's lane order; remove the worktree on every exit path, including the one that raises.
**Evidence:** d53bbce42d6a0d2804d6bd361a8947e80edfdea2 — tests/chains/test_delivery_coordinator.py::test_no_order_the_union_step_could_re_derive_is_the_planner_order, ::test_the_planner_ranking_is_the_order_the_scope_composes_in, ::test_the_lane_that_conflicts_is_the_one_the_ranking_reaches_second, ::test_the_scratch_tree_is_obtained_through_the_git_port_and_removed, ::test_a_raising_check_chain_still_removes_the_composed_tree, ::test_a_lane_with_no_recorded_deliverable_ref_refuses, ::test_a_lane_with_two_recorded_deliverable_refs_refuses, ::test_a_scope_the_planner_ranks_nothing_in_refuses_to_compose pass; gate 9195/25; judged 2026-09-09 (workhorse tier): REFUTED — the Check's removal clause ("the worktree is removed on every path, including the raising one") is not pinned. Mutating `src/kodezart/services/union_composition.py` — setting a leak flag before the merge-conflict `return result` (line 121) and guarding the `finally` (line 155) with `and not leak`, so `remove_worktree` is skipped on the merge-conflict return only — leaves all 8 cited tests passing. The ordering half of the Check does hold: rewriting `src/kodezart/chains/delivery_coordinator.py:74-77` to re-derive the order as `sorted(selection.ready, key=lambda l: (priority_rank(l.issue.priority), l.issue.created_at))` is RED at tip (2 failed / 6 passed, "- a / + c" at `tests/chains/test_delivery_coordinator.py:422`) and GREEN under the pre-commit fixture, so the c/a/d/b fixture genuinely distinguishes consuming the ranking from re-deriving it. Revert protocol ran at d53bbce itself (`git revert --no-commit d53bbce` at c17f5d7 conflicts, UU `tests/chains/test_union_forge_isolation.py`, which c17f5d7 rewrote): under revert 2 of the 8 cited tests do not exist (`test_no_order_the_union_step_could_re_derive_is_the_planner_order`, `test_the_lane_that_conflicts_is_the_one_the_ranking_reaches_second`) and the other 6 pass; restored, `git status --short` empty, 16/16 green at tip.

title: KOD-110-AC-3 — Verifying composes nothing into the world: the forge double exposes no merge capability at all
description:
**Check:** Verifying composes nothing into the world: the step makes no push, no forge merge call and no pull-request state change, every pull request is still open when it returns, and what carries this is structural — the union step holds no forge port at all (only the git port and the check-chain runner), and the forge query port and its double expose no merge capability, so a merge call cannot type-check against the port. The audit terminal's read-only PR lifecycle reader is a separate port with no merge authority and is outside this criterion (ruling <issue id="ecb04c93-2d79-4938-aa98-d3f4856116a3" href="https://linear.app/duckburg/issue/KOD-778/ruling-the-no-merge-state-premise-kod-110-ac-3-rests-on-is-the-audit">KOD-778</issue>); the union never consumes it. (V · property 2)
**Do:** Keep the union step read-only against the forge — no push, no merge call, no pull-request state change, every pull request still open on return; give the forge query port and its double no merge capability, so a merge call cannot type-check against the port. Do not add a merge-state reader to the union step or to the forge query port.
**Evidence:** c17f5d71ce95a94d0fd63f74ee6aa467cce01dad — tests/chains/test_union_forge_isolation.py::test_every_exit_of_the_union_step_leaves_every_ref_identical, ::test_the_union_step_holds_no_forge_collaborator_at_all, ::test_the_holdings_walk_reaches_a_collaborator_inside_a_container, ::test_no_module_the_union_step_reaches_asks_a_pull_request_anything, ::test_the_union_steps_own_modules_name_the_merge_state_reader_nowhere, ::test_the_query_ports_and_their_doubles_expose_no_merge_capability[PRStateReader|DeliveryProbe], ::test_the_forge_predicate_recognises_every_forge_double pass; gate 9196/25; judged 2026-09-09 (workhorse tier): REFUTED — the headline clause ("the step makes no push, no forge merge call and no pull-request state change") is not pinned against a best-effort publish. Inserting, immediately before the merge-conflict `result = UnionCompositionResult(` return in `src/kodezart/services/union_composition.py`, a `try: await self._git.push(worktree, "union")` / `except Exception: pass`, all 8 cited tests PASS (8 passed); same with `except BaseException` (8 passed). Only the bare, unswallowed publish goes RED (1 failed). The battery's sole witness for push/merge_branch/delete_remote_branch is the AssertionError `ForbiddenPublisher` raises, and any swallowing wrapper eats it, while the fatal double keeps `refs() == before` true — so "best-effort", which is by definition the swallowing form, is exactly the shape the module's docstring claims the exit battery closes and does not. The mutation is a real publication, not a paper one: the same conflicting scenario run through the production port (`pinned.ObservedGit` / `SubprocessGitService`, `git push upstream HEAD:refs/heads/union`) over the real author/remote/observer world left the remote holding c076e21d9c42bcb2d33edae6875aeeea253a5eda refs/heads/union.

title: KOD-110-AC-7 — A check-chain runner port with a subprocess adapter, its wall-clock bound a KODEZART_-prefixed config field
description:

The configured per-step timeout is passed directly to the runner; a non-default value changes actual command timeout behavior. Stable process-group cleanup cadence remains an adapter-owned constant, with no configurable cleanup-poll field. (gen · S1-U2)
**Do:** Add the runner as a port in `core/protocols.py`, taking an ordered step sequence and a working directory and returning the failed step names with each step's captured output; add a subprocess adapter beside the git one, and one `AppConfig` field for the per-step wall-clock bound with its `KODEZART_`-prefixed environment name. Pass the validated wall-clock timeout as a narrow value to the adapter. Retain ordered execution, partial output and complete process-group cleanup through repeated cancellation. Remove the cleanup polling setting and refuse its retired input; its stable cadence remains in the adapter.
**Evidence:** — (sha · test names · session/comment ids)

**Plan amendment · 2026-09-08:** <issue id="a35bb59e-e287-4baa-9ddf-0cc099bfd07c" href="https://linear.app/duckburg/issue/KOD-744/v03-architecture-simplification-plan-typed-privacy-focused-settings">KOD-744</issue>/745/468 retire the blanket literal ban. title: Ruling: the no-merge-state premise KOD-110-AC-3 rests on — is the audit lane's PR lifecycle reader an argued exception
description:
**Outcome:** the ruling is a dated comment on this issue and <issue id="cdf9af2c-05cf-47cb-8021-abce46dd8726" href="https://linear.app/duckburg/issue/KOD-589/kod-110-ac-3-verifying-composes-nothing-into-the-world-the-forge">KOD-589</issue> is unblocked.

**Fork:** <issue id="cdf9af2c-05cf-47cb-8021-abce46dd8726" href="https://linear.app/duckburg/issue/KOD-589/kod-110-ac-3-verifying-composes-nothing-into-the-world-the-forge">KOD-589</issue>'s Check rests on "no port at the comparison base declares a merge-state reader and the parent lane forbids adding one", and its Do says "Do not add a merge-state reader". The union step satisfies every operative clause on its own — it holds only the git port and the check-chain runner, pushes nothing, and the forge port and its double expose no merge attribute. But the tip adds exactly such a reader for the audit terminal: `PRStateReader.read_pr_state` → `PRState.lifecycle` with `PRLifecycle.MERGED` (`core/protocols.py`, `adapters/github_api.py`, consumer `services/audit_terminal.py`), added at `3f57793` and absent from trunk. The criterion's global premise is therefore false at the tip while its local behaviour holds.

**Options:**

1. The premise is scoped to the union step and its own doubles: the audit lane's lifecycle reader is an argued exception, and <issue id="cdf9af2c-05cf-47cb-8021-abce46dd8726" href="https://linear.app/duckburg/issue/KOD-589/kod-110-ac-3-verifying-composes-nothing-into-the-world-the-forge">KOD-589</issue> is Done on the operative clauses already verified.
2. The premise is global: the reader violates it, and either the criterion or the reader must be restated — without deleting legitimate audit evidence or inventing a union merge capability.

**Pinned interim:** option 1, scoped narrowly — the union step holds no forge port and its double exposes no merge attribute; nothing further is built on the wider reading this wave.

**Rules:** ORGANIZE pass

**Source:** the [code-grounded grooming · verified at 2d4ff63] comment `798c8ed4` and the [v0.3 fresh implementation audit · 2026-09-08] comment `c220d8ed` on <issue id="cdf9af2c-05cf-47cb-8021-abce46dd8726" href="https://linear.app/duckburg/issue/KOD-589/kod-110-ac-3-verifying-composes-nothing-into-the-world-the-forge">KOD-589</issue>; the lane summary `923e4f80` on <issue id="6655d02b-7b49-4f6c-a020-cd9bd877c9d5" href="https://linear.app/duckburg/issue/KOD-110/union-verification-whether-a-scopes-open-prs-compose-is-unobservable">KOD-110</issue>.

**Done when:** the ruling is recorded here as a dated comment and mirrored as a [ruling] reply on the source comment.
